title: Universal Orlando welcomes new celebrity hot dog stand
summary:
By Robert Niles: CityWalk's new celebrity hot dog stand opens this weekend in Orlando.

Universal Orlando has announced a Saturday grand opening for Fat One's Hot Dogs & Italian Ice, which takes over the former Hot Dog Hall of Fame space on CityWalk.

Founded by *Nsync member Joey Fatone, Fat One's previously had a location at the Florida Mall. The CityWalk location will feature a menu of nine topped hot dogs, including the eponymous The Fat One, a footlong hot dog topped with roasted pork, pepperoni, chili beans, cheddar cheese sauce, red onion sauce, pop fries, and chives.

The first 100 guests in line on Saturday morning will get a free hot dog served by Fatone himself.

Also on Saturday, Universal Orlando CityWalk will celebrate the 10th anniversary of The Toothsome Chocolate Emporium & Savory Feast Kitchen from 3-6pm, with an interactive chocolate dipping station and a Toothsome 10th Anniversary Milkshake available for purchase.

title: Rope Drop: Who's ready for a haunt?
summary:
By Robert Niles: This weekend is the big one for theme park haunt events, with Halloween season taking over parks across the country.

But before the scare actors hit the streets, theme park fans this week will welcome the official debut of the Fast & Furious Hollywood Drift roller coaster at Universal Studios Hollywood on Wednesday. Watch the site Tuesday for coverage of the grand opening celebration and our review of Universal's fastest-ever coaster.

Down the road in Anaheim, it's Gay Days at the Disneyland Resort this week, from September 18 through the 20th.

Now for the Halloween stuff. The industry's original after-hours haunt event returns on Thursday with the debut of 2026's Knott's Scary Farm - so watch for our coverage on Friday. Elsewhere in California, Six Flags Fright Fest kicks off Friday at Magic Mountain, along with Queen Mary's Dark Harbor, Los Angeles Haunted Hayride in Griffith Park, and Festival Fright Nights at Winchester Mystery House up the coast in San Jose. On Saturday, Legoland California starts its Brick-or-Treat, while Six Flags Discovery Kingdom kicks off its Oktoberfest.

Around the country, Cedar Point HalloWeekends starts Thursday, followed by Kings Dominion Halloween Haunt and Six Flags Great Adventure Fright Fest on Friday, and Six Flags Great America Fright Fest on Saturday.

Planning a trip?

Here are the current refurbishment schedules from Disneyland, Walt Disney World and Universal Orlando.

Indiana Jones Adventure is closed at Disneyland, with no reopening date.
September 14: Mad Tea Party closes at Disneyland, with no reopening date.
September 14-16: Tom Sawyer Island closes at Disneyland.
September 15-20: The Untrainable Dragon closes at Universal Epic Universe.
September 21-24: Sailing Ship Columbia closes at Disneyland.
October 26: Volcano Bay closes for the season, with a planned return on or before April 1, 2027.
November 2: Tiana's Bayou Adventure closes at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom, with no reopening date.
November 3: Animal Actors on Location closes permanently at Universal Studios Florida.
November 20: Jurassic Park River Adventure reopens at Islands of Adventure.
January 4 - February 2, 2027: Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges closes at Islands of Adventure.
January 25 - February 4, 2027: Fyre Drill closes at Universal Epic Universe.
February 8-19, 2027: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey closes at Islands of Adventure.
Universal's Horror Make-Up Show is closed at Universal Studios Florida. Estimated reopening in winter 2026.
Carousel of Progress is closed at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom. New show debuts in 2027.

title: Walk Time: Happy birthday to Hong Kong Disneyland
summary:
By Robert Niles: In theme parks and entertainment, "walk time" is the name for the final paid minutes of your shift, when you gather your stuff and start heading home. At Theme Park Insider, "Walk Time" is our weekend look back at the past seven days in theme park news.

Happy 21st birthday today to Hong Kong Disneyland, which first opened to guests on September 12, 2005.

Several theme park haunts have opened this weekend, including Hersheypark Dark Nights and Howl-O-Scream at SeaWorld and Busch Gardens parks across the country. If anyone would like to share a trip report from any of these events, we'd love to read it over on the discussion forum.

Six Flags dominated this news this week, with its announcements of the new Thrill Glider coming to Magic Mountain, its purchase of ArieForce One, and a new monthly payment plan for season passes. Jake and I ripped into that last one on the Theme Park Insider Podcast this week.

At Walt Disney World, the resort this week showed off to invited reporters its new The Magic of Disney Animation area at Disney's Hollywood Studios. In case you missed it, here are our stories:

  • Step into The Magic of Disney Animation at Disney World
  • The pre-show is the star in Disney's new studio show
  • Olaf draws a new home for animation at Walt Disney World

Looking ahead, Disney also announced dates for its first two festivals in 2027: The EPCOT International Festival of the Arts will run January 15 - March 1, while the next EPCOT International Flower & Garden Festival will run from March 10 to May 31.

Finally, this week I spoke with the leaders of the team that is bringing The Wizarding World of Harry Potter to Yas Island in Abu Dhabi. The expansion of Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi is now under construction for an estimated completion in 2029. Find out what Miral CEO Dr. Mohamed Abdalla Al Zaabi and Warner Bros. Discovery President Global Experiences & Studio Operations Simon Robinson had to say in my interview with them.

title: Olaf draws a new home for animation at Walt Disney World
summary:
By myhandsdontscan: Animated storytelling is the foundation of The Walt Disney Company. Animated shorts paved the way for feature animation, a music company, live-action features, television specials, theme parks, cruise lines, and now streaming services. The theme parks may now be Disney�s current cash cow, but animation will always be the cornerstone of its flywheel.

It�s a no-brainer, then, to have animation activities featured in the theme parks to pay tribute to this legacy and inspire the next generation of animators. This manifested at Walt Disney World in the form of Hollywood Studios� Animation Academy (drawing classes led by working Disney Animators), another Animation Academy in DisneyQuest (featuring digital sketch pads), and finally The Animation Experience at Conservation Station (drawing animal characters in Animal Kingdom after hopping aboard the Wildlife Express).

After the revamp of Conservation Station to home �Bluey�s Wild World,� the Walt Disney World parks have been absent an animation experience. That is, until the opening of The Magic of Disney Animation at Disney's Hollywood Studios.

This new experience marries both foundational components, animation and storytelling, of the studio that was �all started by a Mouse.�

But in this case it all starts with a snowman.


Entrance to �Olaf Draws!�

�Olaf Draws!� is the new interactive sketching show inside The Magic of Disney Animation. In this experience guests learn, alongside a wonderfully devious animatronic Olaf (who has seemingly taken over the Animation Academy), how to draw a Disney character from a rotating selection of 9 different artists from the studio�many of them drawing characters they helped create.

The list of available characters and their respective animators are:

  • Mickey Mouse, with Dan Abraham
  • Minnie Mouse, with Hyun Min Lee
  • Donald Duck, with Austin Traylor
  • Genie, with Eric Goldberg
  • Moana, with Samantha Vilfort
  • Stitch, with Fawn Veerasunthorn
  • Olaf, with Trent Correy
  • Ursula, with Michael Woodside
  • Judy Hopps & Nick Wilde, with Byron Howard

Guests are seated in spacious animators� desks and are provided sturdy pages of drawing paper and cups full of sketching pencils. Screens are set up around the desks, making it easy to follow along with the animators in their pre-recorded interactions.


The auditorium of �Olaf Draws!�

When the show starts, the animatronic Olaf comes to life and shortly begins interacting with one of the animators. This is a great animatronic with fluid and expressive movements, a nice �plus-up� from what could have been an otherwise screen-guided experience.

Throughout the instruction Olaf and the animator exchange delightful barbs (this is Josh Gad at his unhinged best), adding a bit of levity and chance for some of the slower drawers in the audience (me) to catch up. I found Olaf funny without being annoying or overused.

Each session lasts around 11 minutes, and I found it pretty easy to follow along for most characters. Though I will admit the speed with some of the more involved characters like Genie was a bit fast for an artistically challenged person who struggles to draw stick figures and abstract art. But it was nevertheless enjoyable. And the animators must know what they�re doing because my sketches actually turned out looking like something resembling the characters. We were even given a mailing tube afterwards for keeping our sketches safe.


I offer Eric Goldberg my sincerest apologies.

But it�s in the moments of pause where the show really shines. The animators get a chance to talk about what inspired them to get into animation or why a certain character resonates with them. They aren�t just teaching you how to draw Mickey Mouse, they�re telling a story about why Mickey Mouse is so resonant.

It�s these personal stories from the animators that justify the pre-recordings. Sure, live animators can provide live feedback, but there�s something remarkable about watching Eric Goldberg draw The Genie (and go toe-to-toe with Olaf to boot). By all means mourn the loss of live animators in the parks, but Disney was able to create a wholly new experience that weaves together animation and storytelling in a seamless experience.

And that�s worth melting for.

�Olaf Draws!� opens with The Art of Disney Animation September 14. Virtual waitlists may be used as needed.

title: The pre-show is the star in Disney's new studio show
summary:
By myhandsdontscan: How do you create an engaging attraction from an animated short guests can watch anytime on Disney+? You make it come alive.

Once Upon A Studio, the Emmy-award winning animated short celebrating 100 years of Disney Animation, was used as inspiration for The Magic of Disney Animation area at Hollywood Studios. Animated characters hop out of their films and drawings and into our world.

That same principle applies to this screening of Once Upon a Studio. The short plays inside a dedicated theater within The Magic of Disney Animation. During portions of the film, animated portraits on both sides of the screen come to life, rushing to be in Mickey�s group photo, adding an extra layer of interaction as well as easter eggs for the repeat viewers to spot.

Once Upon A Studio is worthy of its praise � it hits all the emotional and comedic beats without any fat to trim. But the real treat is actually in the pre-show.

Here, portraits of characters come to life on the wall with PhotoPass opportunities and interactive games. Guests can inflate balloons with Baymax or rock the boat with the Kakamora from �Moana.� After completing the tasks, guests can then strike a pose and get a picture taken with the animated characters. The games also have an element of replay-ability with a scoring system.

This pre-show room will surely be a hit for kids � the waiting doesn�t feel like waiting, and if you�ve already seen Once Upon A Studio, it might be better than the theater experience itself.

Once Upon A Studio will offer guests the perfect gateway to The Magic of Disney Animation experience, which opens September 14.

title: Six Flags introduces its new Thrill Glider for 2027
summary:
By Robert Niles: Well, they did it. Six Flags Magic Mountain just did the most Six Flags thing. The name for the park's first-of-its-kind 2027 Vekoma Thrill Glider roller coaster will be...

Thrill Glider.

Magic Mountain today revealed the name and stats for its next roller coaster, which is now under construction near Looney Tunes Land on the site of the former Golden Bear Theater. Thrill Glider will be 3,380 feet long, with multiple launches and a top speed of 50 mph. The coaster will top out at 107 feet and feature five inversions: a wing-over, zero-g roll, overbanked stall turn, barrel roll, and upward barrel roll.

And Six Flags has a story for this 80-second adventure, too.

Riders are visiting The Futurist Pavilion, a showcase for QuantumPulse Propulsion Systems, which has discovered a new energy source called PSR B417. hexagonal collectors embedded into the hillside collect PSR B417 from distant pulsars.

"Once launched, the power of PSR B417 will be felt firsthand as the vehicles soar above the landscape through sweeping maneuvers, sudden dives and weightless moments that simulate piloting a high-speed hovercycle powered by tomorrow's technology," Six Flags said in its press release.


Image courtsy Six Flags

"Thrill Glider is more than a new attraction. It is the latest milestone in Six Flags Magic Mountain's renaissance and a reflection of the park's enduring role as an industry innovator," Park President Brian Oerding said. "With a decades-long reputation for introducing record-breaking attractions and genre-defining rides, Magic Mountain is uniquely positioned to pioneer an entirely new coaster category and bring Thrill Glider to life."

Thrill Glider will have a minimum height of 48 inches to ride.

title: Step into The Magic of Disney Animation at Disney World
summary:
By myhandsdontscan: What to do with Animation Courtyard? That was the question that drove Walt Disney Imagineering to reimagine The Magic of Disney Animation at Disney's Hollywood Studios, which opens officially September 14th.

The Emmy Award-winning 100th anniversary short Once Upon A Studio was chosen to give the area a sense of place. Rather than simply providing a screening of the short film, the concept was used as inspiration for the entire land, allowing animated characters to come alive and guests the opportunity to jump inside the stories they love.

As the story of the land goes, similar to the "Once Upon A Studio" short, when the animators are out to lunch the animated Disney characters have taken over and are hosting an open house.


WDAS characters are throwing an open house while the animators are out to lunch.

Creativity, exceptional place-making, and a cornucopia of easter eggs and details are overflowing in The Magic of Disney Animation, which is the final phase to The Walt Disney Studios area in Hollywood Studios. Everywhere you look, there are props, trinkets, and items from the 65-film catalog of Disney Animation.

The Imagineers collaborated with veteran Disney animator Eric Goldberg and "Once Upon A Studio" director Dan Abraham to bring the short, and The Magic of Disney Animation, to life. They wanted to ensure that they celebrated the 100-year history of artists, while inspiring the next generation of animators.

There is a reverence to what came before without being beholden to it. In "Once Upon A Studio" and in the revitalized Magic of Disney Animation experience, the artists pay tribute to "Back To Neverland," a short starring Robin Williams and Walter Cronkite that played before the old Magic of Disney Animation tour that opened alongside Hollywood Studios. This short is what inspired many working Disney animators to chase their dreams and get into the business, with Dan Abraham sharing that he used to work in Hollywood Studios and could recite "Back To Neverland" from memory after doing the attraction again and again.

In the short, Robin Williams is transformed into one of Peter Pan�s Lost Boys. This animated Lost Boy makes a cameo in "Once Upon A Studio," and is referenced several times in the new Magic of Disney Animation, including one of the characters holding up the "Open House" sign.

Eric Goldberg, animator of the Genie in Aladdin, revealed that Robin Williams�s attire in the short - a Goofy hat and Hawaiian shirt - inspired the look of the Genie at the end of the movie. In fact, Eric Goldberg also revealed he is now the owner of the original Hawaiian shirt Robin Williams wore in "Back To Neverland."

It�s that level of commitment and passion that breathes through every pore of the new Magic of Disney Animation.

This is a much-needed addition to Hollywood Studios, giving young children, families, or the thrill-adverse an immersive and worthy experience.

The Mickey Avenue section of The Walt Disney Studios area opened in May to pretty big praise. "Disney Jr. Mickey Mouse Clubhouse Live!" opened with the area, giving another option for parents and kids to beat the heat, in addition to the now-connected "Walt Disney Presents" and "The Little Mermaid � A Musical Adventure."

Sculpted characters lurk just about everywhere, providing kids and animation fans numerous "I spy" moments. This outdoor area gives families a chance to sit and rest and kids the chance to play and possibly meet one of the roaming walk-around characters. (Disney was reluctant to state if these outdoor character interactions would continue once the character meet-and-greets within The Magic of Disney Animation opened.)

With a theater show, a drawing walkthrough, a plethora of entertainment, and a themed play area, The Magic of Disney Animation fully fulfills the promise of The Walt Disney Studios land.

Galleries & Studio Store

After walking past the "Open House" sign into glorious climate-controlled A/C goodness, guests can experience the interactive attraction Olaf Draws! To the right are the galleries where characters have loaned their artifacts for display in a museum walkthrough. Think Scrump from Lilo & Stitch, Maui�s hook from Moana, and Rapunzel�s frying pan from Tangled.


Items 'on loan' to the Gallery from animated characters

Also on display in this area are props, images, and concept art from Disney�s upcoming "Hexed" feature film. This gallery could be a great way to future-proof the experience and maintain relevancy, swapping out art and props for the newest upcoming animated feature.


This area is currently promoting Hexed, but could be an avenue for displaying future Disney Animation Studios films

Past this area is a quaint gift shop, Studio Store, with some exclusive merchandise for the Disney Studios area.


One of the exclusive merchandise items in The Magic of Disney Animation

Circling back around past "Olaf Draws!" is a fish bowl room made for lounging. Comfy seating abounds along with a great view of the meet-and-greet area. The light fixtures, comprised of paint and brushes, add nice cohesive theming.


The fishbowl area is a great location to relax and take in the view

The large open space below consists of different components of the animation process, starting with Visual Development. This area houses Drawn to Wonderland, a life-size Alice in Wonderland play area for kids 6 months to 5 years based on Mary Blair�s concept art.

Drawn to Wonderland

Drawn to Wonderland is separated into two play areas: one for kids 6-23 months, and the other 2 to 5 years old.

The former is fantastic, featuring spacious, playground-like rubber surfacing for little ones to walk and crawl, a couple features for supported walking and play, and generous seating and outlets for parents to recharge.

The latter has an interactive tea party play spot (pull up the tea kettle for a fun surprise), a small jungle gym, a slide for kids (and adults who want to aggravate their sciatica) featuring the Cheshire Cat in the Tulgey Wood (and activated sounds when guests slide down), a spinning activity panel, and an incline ramp maze leading to the Queen of Hearts' castle.


Tea Party play area within Drawn to Wonderland

All in all this is a wonderfully themed play area which makes great strides to cater to a demographic that was previously underserved at Hollywood Studios.

Off the Page!

This section of The Magic of Disney Animation is dedicated to character meet-and-greets and photo opportunities.

We continue through the next steps in the animation process: Story & Layout. Mulan meets in Story, which is decorated with storyboards from Once Upon A Studio while Rapunzel meets in Layout, which takes inspiration from Walt Disney�s multiplane camera.

Both interactions are photographed with a nearby artist cabinet. Guests can then scan their ticket or MagicBand on a cleverly-themed copier to save their PhotoPass photos.


The different components of the animation process. Note the multi-plane camera panes and the themed copier.

The next phase in the process is called Animation. This is divided into Hand-Drawn Animation, featuring Chip 'n' Dale and C.G. Animation, featuring Daisy, Donald, and an oversized tablet, keyboard, and mouse reminiscent of classic 90s/early aughts Disney.

Goofy meets in the Lightning section while Stitch meets in Effects, completing our tour through the animation process.

Across Off the Page! before the preshow to "Once Upon A Studio," guests can view storyboards from famous Disney Animation sequences, including "We Don�t Talk About Bruno" from "Encanto" and "Almost There" from "The Princess and the Frog."

But the real star is the animator�s office with a desk reused from the days of Walt Disney Feature Animation Florida. Tchotchkes and trinkets of every sort line every square inch of this office. Guests could easily spend multiple visits soaking in all the details and still not catch everything this office has to offer.

Stitch can be seen swirling on the animator�s chair. Hei-Hei is rummaging through the trash. Mushu is playing Fix-It Felix Jr. It�s hard not to love this exhibit.


The insanely-detailed animator�s office

Finally, guests arrive at "Once Upon A Studio" and its pre-show.

These experiences can really be done in any order, and Disney has designed this space to have multiple entries and exits, with dedicated entries to both "Once Upon A Studio" and Olaf Draws, to keep congestion at a minimum.

But I can�t help feeling the Platonic ideal order is doing Once Upon A Studio first, to pay tribute to the artistry that built 100 years of Disney, then experience the process of animation with Drawn to Wonderland & Off the Page! before stepping into the animation process yourself in Olaf Draws! and ending with a preview of the next Disney Animation project.

Not every project needs to be a half-billion dollar state-of-the-art E-ticket attraction. Disney wasn�t swinging for a home run here - they were aiming for a double. But they knocked it out of the park. The passion, creativity, and joy Disney brought to this project is infectious.

It�s for that reason that The Magic of Disney Animation is a resounding success.

title: Efteling offers new safety solution for coaster fans
summary:
By Robert Niles: Efteling is offering a new safety solution for thrill ride fans with leg prostheses.

The park's new SafeStrap allows visitors with leg prostheses to ride several park attractions without having to remove their prosthesis. The device will be available starting October 1 for riders on the floorless dive coaster Baron 1898, the Hooghmoed free-fall towers, and the park's swing rides. The new Ravenring attraction also will use the device when that ride opens December 1.


Riders using SafeStrap on Baron 1989. Photo courtesy Efteling

Let's talk about thrill ride restraint systems for a moment. The general concept is to develop a restraint system that can accommodate as many riders as possible while allowing operators to unload, load and dispatch the ride vehicle as quickly as possible.

That typically leads designers to a one-style-for-all solution, where all the seats on a train or ride employ the same system. That makes it easy for operators to load and dispatch, as all they need to do is check that riders have engaged the restraint, whether that's a lap bar, seatbelt, or over-the-shoulders pulldown bar. There's no need to customize the restraint offered for each rider.

Prospective riders who cannot be accommodated by the ride's restraint system would be excluded from the ride. Most often, that means a minimum rider height. But in some cases, that also has meant that people with a leg prosthesis, for example, would not be allowed to ride without removing it, given that the default restraint may not be able to secure the prosthesis.

Efteling's device removes that restriction. But it does so with an extra device that must be put on before the ride can dispatch. The challenge here is whether that has enough of a detrimental effect on load time that it reduces ride capacity to a significant extent.

The percentage of the population with leg prostheses is low - less than 1 percent. And I suspect that the percentage is even lower within the thrill ride community. So the time to get on and off a ride with the SafeStrap might easily get lost in the noise of variance among different hundreds of other riders' natural load and unload times. The downside then to the general population of coaster riders might be low, but the upside to a fan with a prothesis could be huge.

"From the very beginning, we worked together with prosthesis users, healthcare professionals and Efteling to develop a solution that is both safe and practical for users and amusement parks," said India Hoekman, who developed SafeStrap as part of her graduation project at Delft University of Technology. "I find it incredibly special that the product I designed as part of my final-year project is actually being used now."

Following its launch at Efteling, the SafeStrap is now available worldwide to theme parks and prosthetic users. Parks wishing to use the SafeStrap must, in consultation with their own regulatory body, obtain approval for its use on each individual ride.
